thread.title: Spotify: Bundles Can Help Keep Subscribers Around

author: David Marino-Nachison
title: Spotify: Bundles Can Help Keep Subscribers Around
text:
Photo: Spotify By David Marino-Nachison July 26, 2018 11:42 a.m. ET How do you keep people from ducking their Spotify Technology (SPOT) subscriptions for competing services? Maybe by offering them something more than a Spotify subscription.
Barron’s Next 50 company Spotify reported Q2 financial results Thursday morning, turning in premium subscription growth of 40% year-over-year to reach 83 million. The company credited a marketing campaign and family plans—but also an offer that bundles Spotify with streaming video service Hulu. That offer, originally targeted at students, is now available to everyone in the U.S.
Newsletter Sign-up On Thursday, MKM Partners said Spotify bears—MKM has a buy rating and a $200 price target, 4% current levels, on the stock—think ”competing services are 100% substitutive.” (We’ve covered the competitive landscape for Spotify, which includes such companies as Amazon.com (AMZN), Apple (AAPL), a number of times .)
Bundles could combat that. It’s one thing to ditch Spotify, but what if you have to ditch Hulu to do so? That raises the switching cost, literally and figuratively, a number of ways. (Family plans could be said to offer a similar “magnet,” since unsubscribing affects multiple people.) On a conference call with investors, a transcript of which was available on FactSet, Spotify CEO Daniel Ek said churn was down year-over-year.
Spotify isn’t the only streaming music service that likes partnership offers. Fellow Barron’s Next 50 company Pandora Media (P), for example, is part of an AT&T (T) offer; the company, scheduled to report its own quarterly results next week, said it would discuss its deals’ financial effect when it does so.
The competition, of course, has its own options; Amazon includes a level of Amazon Music in Prime. And investors have long wondered whether a kind of “Apple Prime” service might be on the way.
Newsletter Sign-up As for Spotify: “We’re very encouraged by the early results on both launches, both the Hulu student plan and now the Hulu stand-alone plan,” Ek said on the conference call. “This is a huge part of what we’re doing, which is trying to find more ways to bring more value to our members on the subscriber base.”
Is more coming? “We don’t have anything to announce,” Ek said on the call. “But you should look at it as part of our strategy, just like we’ve said before, to look at more ways to add more value for our members.”
Shares of Spotify, up nearly 30% since its early April public offering, rose nearly 4% in Thursday morning trading.
